title: Circular Economy Potential of Winemaking By-Products: Romania in the Context of Major EU Wine Producers
content: Winemaking by-products are rarely quantified and valued at the national level. This study estimates the circular economy potential of grape pomace, seeds, stalks, wine lees and vine shoots in Romania and eight major EU wine producers over 2010–2025, using Eurostat and OIV data, literature-based coefficients in three scenarios, two valorisation pathways and 2025 prices. In 2025, the nine countries generated an estimated 10.35 Mt of by-products (range 6.39–14.30 Mt), of which Romania accounted for 487 kt. Romania’s apparent wine yield (480 L t⁻¹) was significantly lower than that of seven of the other eight countries (p &lt; 0.001), suggesting that part of its by-product flow is not captured by recorded wine production. Vine shoots were the largest stream in every country (44–64%) and the main source of uncertainty. Pelletising stalks and vine shoots would yield 63.2 M EUR in Romania, while an integrated cascade adding distillation, seed oil, tartrate and compost would yield 78.5 M EUR (30.7–137.7 M EUR), or 71.7 M EUR if limited to recorded processing, with grape seed oil providing about 80% of the additional value. Recovering by-products from small producers and measuring pruning biomass are key conditions for realising this potential.
